models.name: shopping_mall_customers
models.description:
Primary actor table for registered shopping platform customers with email/password authentication. Stores core account credentials, profile information, and audit fields for account lifecycle management.

Handles customer registration, authentication, and profile management through email verification and password complexity requirements. Each customer record serves as the root identity for all platform interactions including order history, wishlist items, and address management.

Includes mandatory email validation and password complexity rules for security compliance. Supports email verification workflows and preserves order history even after account deletion (marked as 'deleted user'). Account deletion triggers session termination and profile preservation for historical reference.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Customer's verified email address used for login, verification, and communication. Must be unique across all customers and comply with standard email format requirements.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure hash of customer's password stored during registration. Used for authentication validation. Never stores plain passwords.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Customer's preferred name for public profile display. Allows alphanumeric characters with max 50 characters under real-time validation.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Customer's contact phone number stored in international E.164 format. Supports country code detection and validation standards for all regions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of customer account creation. Automatically set to current time during registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification. Automatically updated during profile changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when account was deleted (soft delete). Preserves account history while preventing new activity.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for customer authentication with access and refresh token support, validated for 15-minute expiration period.

Stores connection context for customer login sessions including IP address, connection URL, and referrer information. All sessions are time-bound with mandatory expiration to enhance security.

Each session is linked to a customer's active account and represents a unique login event. The table follows session logging best practices with timestamped activity records for audit and security monitoring. Session records are appended-only with no deletions allowed.

All sessions include necessary metadata for connection context, enabling effective session tracking, user activity analysis, and security threat detection.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer session owner's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: User's IP address at the time of session creation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the connection request.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from which the user arrived at the system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires for security purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for customer account confirmation during registration.

Stores tokens sent via email to verify customer account ownership during the initial registration process. Each token has a specific expiration period to ensure security against brute force attacks.

Tokens are created when a customer requests account verification, then validated against the customer's identity when the user clicks the verification link. The token is discarded after successful verification or expiration.

Provides a security layer preventing malicious registrations while maintaining user privacy.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer record this verification belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token string for email link. Follows security best practices (256-bit AES encrypted).

plainFields.name: expiration
plainFields.description: Token expiration time. Must be within 24 hours of token creation for security compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Token creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Token last update timestamp (used for tracking attempts).

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when token was successfully verified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for security auditing and token management.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for customer account recovery with expiration timestamps.

Stores generated tokens securely linked to customer accounts, ensuring they are invalid after specified expiration periods. Each token is uniquely associated with a customer for safe, time-limited access to the password reset workflow. Maintains data integrity through expiration management without user intervention.

foreignFields.name: customers_id
foreignFields.description: Customer responsible for password reset request.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique token for password reset validation. Generated using cryptographically secure random string

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when password reset token expires, preventing stale attempts

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Seller accounts requiring administrative approval before platform participation.

Houses authentication credentials including email for login, with password hashing for security. Each account has a status field (pending/approved/rejected) tracking the approval workflow from submission through to platform access.

Sellers cannot access platform features until approved. Seller profile data is managed through separate seller_profile_snapshots table for audit trail, while this table focuses on authentication and status tracking.

Standard temporal fields support historical tracking, and soft delete capability allows for account deactivation without data deletion.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all sellers.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for login authentication. Never stores plain passwords.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current seller account status. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected. Status transitions follow approval workflow rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Seller account creation timestamp. Used for audit trails and new user metrics.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp for seller account information. Used for audit and synchronization.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null indicates active account, timestamp indicates deletion history.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for seller account confirmation during registration, providing secure email validation to prevent fake registrations.

This table stores unique tokens that expire after a set period to confirm seller email addresses before account activation. Each record tracks the verification token's creation, expiration, and usage status. The system automatically deletes expired tokens to maintain security and reduce database bloat.

Tokens are valid for 15 minutes, matching the system-wide authentication token expiration policy. When a token is used to verify an email, the system creates a new seller account with the verified email. Verification attempts are tracked for security monitoring and account recovery analysis.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller's email address for verification. Must be unique and valid format.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to email for confirmation. Randomly generated with high entropy.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification token expires. Must be 15 minutes after creation.

plainFields.name: is_used
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the verification token has been successfully used to confirm email. Never null.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification record was last modified (e.g., when token is marked as used).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification record was deleted (soft delete). Nullable for tracking historical activity.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description:
Seller password reset tokens with expiration for secure password recovery workflow.

Stores tokens generated for seller password reset requests, with expiration timestamps to ensure security.
Each token is associated with a specific seller's account and includes a flag to indicate if it's been used (to prevent reuse).

Tokens with expiration are automatically invalidated after a set period to protect against session hijacking.
Each password reset token is valid for a standard 30 minutes from the time of creation, after which it expires and becomes unusable.

The token value itself is stored securely as a hashed string, not as plaintext, to prevent security breaches if the database is compromised.

This table is a subsidiary entity, as it's managed through the seller's authentication API and doesn't require direct user creation or independent API operations.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who requested password reset. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: reset_token
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password reset token string.

plainFields.name: expiration
plainFields.description: Password reset token expiration timestamp. Token expires after 30 minutes.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Indicates if the token has been used for password reset. True = token used, False = token available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Token generation timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with elevated privileges for platform management, using email/password authentication. These accounts require email-based login with secure password hashing to provide system-wide administrative capabilities for managing users, content, and platform operations. Each account serves as the primary identity record used across all administrative workflows and permissions systems. The password hash enables secure authentication without storing credentials in plaintext, following industry security best practices for user management systems.

Administrators are distinct from other actor types (customers, sellers) in both capabilities and authentication requirements, forming the foundation for centralized platform governance and control mechanisms.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator email address used for login authentication. Must be unique across all administrator accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password used for authentication. Stored in hashed form only, never in plaintext.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account details were last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was logically deleted. Used for soft delete capability while preserving audit trails.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator accounts with expiration timestamps.

Stores temporary tokens used in the administrator password reset workflow. Each token is associated with a specific administrator and has a time-limited validity period for security.

The token is generated with cryptographic randomness for security purposes. Each token is used once and expires after a fixed period (typically 1 hour) to prevent security risks.

This table does not store password hashes or other sensitive data - only temporary tokens with expiration information. Soft deletion is not typically used for password reset tokens as they expire naturally.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Corresponding administrator's {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Temporary cryptographic token generated for password reset. Must be unique for security reasons.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires. Must be greater than created_at.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions
models.description:
Seller authentication session management for secure login tracking. Stores connection context and lifecycle metrics for seller accounts with JWT token validation. Session data includes connection metadata, expiration policies, and temporal auditing for security monitoring.

Session records track seller login details for security auditing and lifecycle tracking. Each session includes IP address, connection URL, referrer, and creation timestamps. Session expiration is enforced by NOT NULL expired_at field following security standards. These records support session management workflows while maintaining audit trails for security compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller account's {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL used for session establishment.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Source referring URL for session creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session expires (security requirement: never null).

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens that support secure administrator account registration and confirmation. Provides temporary token-based verification for new administrator accounts to prevent unauthorized registration attempts and ensure valid email ownership during onboarding. Each verification token is associated with a specific administrator account being registered and is valid for a limited time period. The token is automatically marked as used upon successful email verification and expires as per defined time limit.

Verification tokens cannot be reused once verified, and expiration prevents unauthorized use of expired tokens. This ensures the security of the administrator registration process while maintaining an audit trail of verification attempts.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Associated administrator account's {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token string used in email confirmation link.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification token expires, after which it can no longer be used.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when verification token was successfully used for account activation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this verification record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was soft deleted (inactive).

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
Session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh token support. Stores connection metadata and session lifecycle timestamps for audit trail and security management.

Append-only pattern for login events with expiration tracking. Managed through authentication workflows, not direct user CRUD operations. Follows the session table pattern with all required fields and index pattern.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrators's {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation time

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration time

models.name: shopping_mall_channels
models.description:
Sales channels representing different points of product accessibility including online stores, mobile applications, and physical retail locations. Each channel has branding configurations, operational settings, and status tracking for business management. Supports channel-level branding and configuration without requiring relationships to other entities.

Channels can be enabled or disabled through status transitions, with 'archived' status indicating historical tracking for auditing purposes. All configuration changes are managed through the channel entity itself without dependency on other components.

Branding configurations follow a standard URI format for centralized style management, allowing consistent visual presentation across all channel interfaces.

plainFields.name: channel_name
plainFields.description: Name of the sales channel (e.g., 'Online Store', 'Mobile App'). Must be unique across all channels.

plainFields.name: branding_config
plainFields.description: URI for channel branding configuration (logo, colors, etc.). Points to centralized configuration storage.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current operational status: 'active' (operational), 'inactive' (temporarily disabled), or 'archived' (historical record).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when channel was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when channel was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when channel was marked for deletion (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_sections
models.description: Hierarchical sections within sales channels for organizing content and products at multiple levels. Sections can be nested to form a tree structure, allowing for flexible categorization of content and product listings across different sales channels. All sections are associated with a specific channel and support a hierarchical ordering where sections can have parent sections for nested organizational structures.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_channel_id
foreignFields.description: The sales channel to which this section belongs.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: The parent section for hierarchical nesting, if this section is a child of another section.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The title of the section used for display purposes in the user interface.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: A unique code identifier for the section, used to reference the section in code and other internal systems.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was soft-deleted (not null denotes deletion).

models.name: shopping_mall_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and feature flags for the entire platform.

Stores key-value pairs of system settings that control platform behavior, features, and operational parameters. Each configuration key is unique and represents a specific aspect of the platform's runtime behavior. Values can be simple strings, JSON objects, or complex structures depending on the configuration's purpose.

Configurations enable dynamic system behavior adjustments without code deployment, such as toggling features on/off, setting thresholds, or defining runtime parameters. All configuration changes create audit records for tracking system modifications.

The table follows a simple key-value structure with an intuitive key naming pattern to facilitate configuration management by administrators. Configuration changes are captured with precise timestamps and modification histories to support audit trails.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key name used to identify and retrieve the setting.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Current value for the configuration setting. Accepts string, JSON, or complex data structures as strings.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of what this configuration key controls and its potential values.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was marked for deletion (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_addresses
models.description:
Maintains current shipping addresses for customers, including street, city, postal code, and country fields with required validation for shipping.

Stores customer's active shipping addresses that are used for order fulfillment. Each address must be associated with a customer account and is part of the customer's profile data. Allows creation, update, and soft deletion of address entries.

Addresses are validated for format and completeness before storage. The current status allows active use for shipping, while soft deletion preserves historical records for order history and user reference.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer's identifier. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: street
plainFields.description: Full street address including building number and street name.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: Name of the city for the shipping address.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal code (ZIP code) for the shipping address, validated by country.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name for the shipping address, typically using two-letter ISO codes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the address was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the address was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the address was soft-deleted (nullable).

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_address_histories
models.description:
Address modification history tracking.

Captures every modification to customer addresses including timestamp, user who made the change, and historical details.
This table records the moment a customer updates their shipping address, preserving the state at that point in time.
The address reference ensures we can retrieve the historical data even when the current address changes.
Each entry in this table is immutable - it records a timestamped event of a specific change.

foreignFields.name: customer_address_id
foreignFields.description: The main address record associated with this change event.

foreignFields.name: changed_by_id
foreignFields.description: Identifies the customer who performed the address modification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this address change occurred.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this snapshot was created (immutable).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this snapshot was marked as deleted (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_products
models.description:
Core product catalog with name, description, category, and pricing information.

Manages product listings for the shopping mall platform, allowing sellers to publish and manage products for customer visibility.

Product data includes name, description, category, base price, and status tracking (active, inactive). Each product has its own unique identifier and timestamps for creation and updates.

Products are categorized via the product_categories table, enabling efficient product grouping and navigation. Soft deletion is supported for content moderation without removing access to historical data.

This table follows 3NF normalization principles with all non-key attributes depending directly on the primary key.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Product category identifier. {@link shopping_mall_product_categories.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name for display to customers. Required field, minimum 3 characters, maximum 255 characters.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Product description providing details about the product features and specifications. Must be at least 10 characters long.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Base price of the product in USD before any discounts. Must be greater than $0.01.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the product. Valid statuses: active, inactive, out_of_stock.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was marked for deletion (soft delete). Null if not deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variants
models.description:
Product variant data for specific merchandise options with unique SKU and stock quantity tracking.

Stores individual product variants including SKU (formatted as SKU-XXXXX), price override, and current stock quantity. Each variant belongs to a single product in the catalog and reflects the product's options (e.g., color, size) at the time of the variant's creation.

Variants can have price overrides from the base product price, which allows flexibility without modifying the main product's price. Stock quantity represents available units for sales, must be positive.

The table supports snapshot preservation for historical tracking of variant changes, maintaining audit trails for product management.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced product's {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: sku
plainFields.description: Unique product variant identifier formatted as SKU-XXXXX. Must follow SKU format consistency across all variants.

plainFields.name: price_override
plainFields.description: Optional override price for this variant. If null, uses base price from parent product.

plainFields.name: stock_quantity
plainFields.description: Number of available units for this variant. Must be greater than zero to indicate available inventory.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when this variant record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this variant record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when record was marked for deletion (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_product_view_stats
models.description:
Tracks product view counts and analytics metrics for recommendation engines and performance analysis.

Records historical product view data to improve recommendation algorithms and measure marketing effectiveness. Each entry represents a product view count at specific points in time with context about the product.

This table is populated through tracking logic in the frontend application that records view events. Data persists for analytics and reporting without modification or deletion. The relationship to products is maintained through foreign keys, preserving historical context.

Product view data is immutable once recorded - new entries are created as views occur, rather than updating existing records. The view count is stored as raw data, never calculated dynamically at query time.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product being viewed. {@link shopping_mall_products.id.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Total count of views for the product at this point in time. Represents cumulative views since last record.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view data was recorded. Indicates the point in time the view count was captured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view data record was last updated. For analytics, this typically matches created_at as records are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was soft-deleted (for retention policies). Not used for active analytics.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical record capturing the exact state of product data at the time of modification. Preserves product name, description, price, category, status, and the seller who made the change for audit verification and historical reference. All snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted to maintain data integrity.

Snapshots provide the complete context of product state at any point in time. Each snapshot is tied to the product, seller, and category as they existed during the modification event. The name reflects the product's state at that moment, description provides context for the changes, price and status show the active product configuration during the modification period. The created_at timestamp enables precise historical tracking of when changes occurred.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that was modified. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who modified the product. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_category_id
foreignFields.description: Product category at the time of modification. {@link shopping_mall_product_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name at the exact time of modification, required for historical accuracy and user-friendly context.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Product description at the exact time of modification, capturing the state as recorded during the change event.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Product price in USD at the time of modification, used for sales auditing and historical pricing analysis.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current product status at time of modification (e.g., 'active', 'inactive', 'deleted'). Reflects state as it should have been visible to users during the modification period.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Precise timestamp when the modification occurred, including timezone for global consistency.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_histories
models.description:
Tracks changes to product variant stock quantities with timestamps, delta values, and reason descriptions.

Records every addition or subtraction to product variant stock, including restock events and order fulfillments. Each history entry is tied to a specific product variant and maintains a full audit trail of inventory changes.

The system automatically creates a new history record whenever stock quantities are modified (by restock actions or sales processing), capturing the exact delta amount, reason for the change, and timestamps.

This table supports inventory tracking and reporting without requiring direct user interaction, making it appropriate for subsidiary status.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant this inventory change applies to. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: delta
plainFields.description: Quantity change amount. Positive for stock increases (restocks), negative for decreases (sales).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Description of why the inventory change occurred (e.g., 'Restock', 'Order Fulfillment', 'Stock Correction').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when inventory change record was created, automatically populated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when inventory change record was last updated, automatically populated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when record was soft-deleted. Null if not deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_images
models.description:
Product images associated with individual items in the catalog for display on product detail pages. Stores image URLs with upload timestamps and metadata for each product variant. Each image is linked to a specific product through a foreign key.

Images are managed through product management workflows, not independently. Metadata is now atomic with format, dimensions, and accessibility text stored as separate fields for proper normalization.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Associated product's {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: URL to the product image file. Must be a valid public URL.

plainFields.name: upload_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

plainFields.name: image_format
plainFields.description: Image file format (e.g., jpg, png, gif).

plainFields.name: image_width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels.

plainFields.name: image_height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Alternative text for accessibility and image description.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image record was marked as deleted (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_product_categories
models.description:
Product categories for organizing catalog items with hierarchical structure and multi-category support.

Defines the taxonomic structure for product categorization, enabling merchants to organize items within a multi-level taxonomy. Categories can be nested within parent categories to create a hierarchical catalog structure.

Product categories serve as the foundation for product discovery and browsing, allowing customers to navigate the catalog through category trees. Each category contains a unique name and descriptive information that may be used in UI elements and search functionality.

The hierarchical nature allows for both broad and specific category groupings (e.g., electronics > smartphones > flagship models). Multi-category support enables products to appear in multiple relevant categories for improved discoverability without duplicating product data.

foreignFields.name: parent_category_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's identifier. {@link shopping_mall_product_categories.id.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name displayed to customers, must be unique across all categories.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the category used in UI and SEO purposes.

plainFields.name: level
plainFields.description: Hierarchy level within category tree (root = 1, children = level + 1).

plainFields.name: rank
plainFields.description: Relative ordering within same-level categories for display priority.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category was soft deleted (null if active).

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_options
models.description:
Key-value pairs for product variant options (e.g., color, size).

Stores variant option definitions with key (e.g., 'color') and value (e.g., 'red') for product variants. Always associated with a specific product variant and managed through the variant API operations.

This table maintains 1NF compliance by separating key-value pairs into individual rows instead of using JSON arrays. Option values must be valid strings and are always tied to their parent product variant for context.

Option key-value data is never directly managed outside of the variant management process, ensuring data integrity and proper relationships.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The product variant this option belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: option_key
plainFields.description: The name of the variant option (e.g., 'color', 'size').

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: The specific value for the option (e.g., 'red', 'large').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product variant option was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product variant option was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product variant option was soft deleted (null if not deleted).

models.name: shopping_mall_sales_orders
models.description:
Main order records capturing transactions with pricing details at time of purchase.

Tracks customer order transactions including status, delivery details, and reference to order items. Each order is associated with a customer's active session and shipping address. Orders are created when items are added to cart and validated for availability, triggering inventory checks. All order records maintain timestamping for creation, updates, and logical deletion for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: shopping_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who placed the order. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_customer_address_id
foreignFields.description: Shipping address used for this order. {@link shopping_mall_customer_addresses.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current order status. Valid values: pending, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled. Status transitions follow business workflow rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order details were last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order was logically deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_sales_order_items
models.description:
Individual items within orders with variant pricing and quantity details, capturing product information at the time of purchase for historical auditability.

Each order item represents a single product variant purchased by a customer, maintaining the exact product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of transaction. This ensures that order histories remain accurate even if product details change later. Order items are directly managed by customers through their order history and support individual item operations such as cancellation and refund requests.

The order item associates with the parent order through the order_id foreign key, and references the specific product variant at purchase time via product_variant_id. This design supports snapshot preservation for order item changes, with historical state tracking handled by the dedicated snapshot table in this component.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sales_orders_id
foreignFields.description: The order this item belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_sales_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variants_id
foreignFields.description: The product variant at the time of purchase. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased for this variant. Must be positive and cannot be zero.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Price per unit of the variant at the time of purchase. This remains immutable even if the product's list price changes later.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was created (order placement time).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last timestamp when this order item was updated (e.g., during cancellation processing).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was soft-deleted (e.g., during cancellation). NULL indicates active item.

models.name: shopping_mall_sales_order_item_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots capturing order item status transitions for audit and traceability.

This table maintains immutable records of each order item status change, including previous and new status values, who made the change, and the timestamp of the transaction.

Stores complete historical context for every status transition, enabling accurate dispute resolution, sales analytics, and audit trails without impacting current order item data.

All changes to order item status trigger automatic snapshot creation with preserved previous values, ensuring complete chain of custody for all order fulfillment stages.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sales_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The related order item this snapshot refers to. {@link shopping_mall_sales_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: status_before
plainFields.description: Previous status value of the order item before change.

plainFields.name: status_after
plainFields.description: New status value of the order item after change.

plainFields.name: modified_by_actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor that made the change (customer, seller, or admin).

plainFields.name: modified_by_actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the actor that made the change (references specific actor table).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created (status change occurred).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was last modified (should match created_at for snapshots).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was logically deleted; null indicates active record.

models.name: shopping_mall_sales_promotions
models.description:
Promotional structures defining pricing strategies and sales campaigns.

This table stores all defined promotional configurations including percentage discounts, fixed amount reductions, and free shipping offers.
Each promotion has a unique name, type, discount value, and active date range.

Promotions can be activated or deactivated through the interface, maintaining audit trail for all modifications.
Soft deletion is supported for promotion management while preserving historical campaign data.

Multiple active promotions can coexist with the system enforcing rules to prevent overlapping discount conflicts.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Promotion name displayed in admin interface and customer-facing campaigns. Must be unique across all promotions.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of promotion purpose and terms for admin reference.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Promotion type: 'percentage' for percentage discounts, 'fixed' for fixed amount reductions, 'free_shipping' for shipping cost waivers.

plainFields.name: discount_value
plainFields.description: Discount amount as percentage (0.01-99.99) or fixed amount (>$0.01) depending on promotion type.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when promotion becomes active.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when promotion expires and becomes inactive.

plainFields.name: promo_code
plainFields.description: Optional promotional code customers can enter to apply the discount. Must be unique if provided.

plainFields.name: max_usage
plainFields.description: Maximum number of times this promotion can be used. Null means unlimited usage.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the promotion is currently active for customers.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion was soft deleted. Null indicates promotion is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_sales_promo_codes
models.description:
Discount codes and coupon redemption records for promotional execution.

Stores all parameters for defining and managing discount campaigns, including valid duration, usage limits, and discount types. Each code can be used for percentage-based discounts, fixed dollar amounts, or free shipping options. Supports multi-use campaigns and customer-specific usage limits.

Promotional codes maintain full audit history through the snapshot system as part of the sales component, with all business parameters preserved at time of redemption.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The human-readable name of the promotional campaign or code. Used for internal management and customer-facing display.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: The actual discount code used by customers. Must be unique, uppercase alphanumeric with no spaces.

plainFields.name: discount_type
plainFields.description: The type of discount offered. Valid values: 'percentage', 'fixed_amount', 'free_shipping'.

plainFields.name: discount_value
plainFields.description: The value of the discount. For 'percentage', it's 0-100; for 'fixed_amount', it's positive dollar amount; for 'free_shipping', this field is not used and should be null.

plainFields.name: min_purchase_amount
plainFields.description: The minimum purchase amount for code redemption. Null indicates no minimum required.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The date/time when the discount becomes active and can be redeemed.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: The date/time when the discount expires and can no longer be redeemed.

plainFields.name: max_uses
plainFields.description: Total number of times the code can be used across all customers. Null indicates unlimited uses.

plainFields.name: max_uses_per_customer
plainFields.description: Maximum number of times a single customer can use the code. Null indicates no limit.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the discount is currently active. Default: true.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the code was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the code was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the code was soft-deleted. Null if active.

models.name: shopping_mall_carts
models.description:
User cart records for shopping selection before order commitment.

Stores active shopping selections with cart status and customer reference. Carts represent temporary state where users can add/remove items, adjust quantities, and apply discounts before converting to an order. Each cart is associated with a specific customer and has a status indicating its current lifecycle stage (e.g., active, expired).

Carts are automatically expired after a period of inactivity to free up resources. When a customer proceeds to checkout, the cart is transformed into an order record, preserving the cart's contents as order items with snapshots of product details at purchase time.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Associated customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current cart status. Valid values: 'active', 'expired', 'converted_to_order'. Status transitions are managed during the shopping workflow.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart was soft-deleted. Null indicates cart is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Tracks items added to user shopping carts, including product variants, quantities, and prices at time of addition. Each cart item records variant details and current pricing to ensure shopping experience matches transaction context even if product details later change.

Cart items exist as a direct user-managed entity where customers add/remove products and adjust quantities. This requires independent management capabilities including: 
- Updating quantities for existing items
- Removal of specific items without affecting entire cart
- Historical tracking of items added at different times
- Price preservation from add time to cart commitment

The model references active carts (shopping_mall_carts) to associate items with shopping sessions and product variants (shopping_mall_product_variants) for full catalog context.

Snapshots are handled by the cart_snapshots table, so this model focuses on current cart state without historical preservation fields.

foreignFields.name: cart_id
foreignFields.description: Cart that the item belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_carts.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant included in the cart. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of this product variant in the cart. Must be at least 1 and reflect real inventory levels.

plainFields.name: price_at_time
plainFields.description: Price of the product variant at the time it was added to the cart, preserving historical accuracy even if prices change later.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart item was added to the cart.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart item was last modified (e.g., quantity update).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart item was soft-deleted (e.g., when removed from cart).

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical records of cart state changes capturing modification details for audit and traceability purposes.

Stores the complete cart state at the time of modification including all items, their quantities, and prices. Enables detailed tracking of cart changes without interfering with current cart operations. All historical data remains accessible for customer support, order recovery, and system diagnostics.

Provides a full audit trail of cart state transitions (additions, removals, modifications) with timestamps and references to corresponding cart entities. Supports soft deletion for historical record maintenance.

foreignFields.name: cart_id
foreignFields.description: Cart entity this snapshot refers to. {@link shopping_mall_carts.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Deletion timestamp for soft delete.

models.name: shopping_mall_orders
models.description:
Main order records with timestamp, status, and customer reference.

Captures the primary business entity for customer transactions across the platform, recording order state, timestamps, and customer ownership. Each order represents a complete transaction from initial creation to final delivery, maintaining historical context for the order lifecycle.

Orders are created through the checkout process with valid inventory, requiring a shipping address. Order status follows the business workflow: pending → processing → shipped → delivered, with possible cancellation. Each order maintains a unique identifier for tracking across the system.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer reference. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current order status. Values: "pending", "processing", "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled".

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Order creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for order state.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp to preserve historical records.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description:
Line items within orders tracking quantities, prices, and product details at time of purchase.

Each order item is associated with a specific order and product variant snapshot, capturing the exact product state when the order was placed. The status field tracks the current progression through the fulfillment workflow (paid → shipped → delivered → cancelled).

Order items support independent management for customers to view order history, request cancellations, and track fulfillment status across different items in their orders. The product snapshot reference ensures historical accuracy even when product details change post-purchase.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent order. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product snapshot capturing product state at purchase time. {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of variant units purchased. Must be greater than zero.

plainFields.name: price_at_purchase
plainFields.description: Price of variant at time of purchase, for historical accuracy and refund calculations.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current order item status. Valid values: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'. Status transitions follow business workflow rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was soft-deleted. Null indicates active status.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipments
models.description:
Shipping record for order items with carrier details and tracking information.

Tracks the fulfillment status of each order item's shipment. Includes carrier name, tracking number, shipment timestamps, and associated shipping address.

Shipment status is updated to 'shipped' upon creation. Tracking number must be unique per shipment and provided by carrier.

Associated with order items for order status tracking and with customer shipping addresses for delivery logistics.

foreignFields.name: shipping_address_id
foreignFields.description: Customer's shipping address. {@link shopping_mall_customer_addresses.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item being shipped. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: carrier
plainFields.description: Shipping carrier name (e.g., 'USPS', 'DHL', 'FedEx'). Must be a valid carrier service provider.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique carrier tracking number for the shipment. Must be provided by carrier and follow their standard formats.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when shipment was processed and handed to carrier. Must be set when shipment is created.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery
plainFields.description: Projected delivery date based on carrier's shipping schedule.

plainFields.name: actual_delivery
plainFields.description: Actual delivery timestamp when item is confirmed as received by customer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shipment was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to shipment details.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when soft deletion was requested (for audit trail).

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Refund requests made by customers for specific order line items. Each refund request includes a reason for the refund, current approval status, and timestamps for tracking the refund process.

Customers can request refunds for items that are in the 'shipped' or 'delivered' status, but not for items that are still processing or on hold. All refund requests require a valid reason and must be reviewed by a seller before approval or rejection.

The refund process follows the system's order status workflow, with automatic updates to order item status upon final approval or rejection of the refund request.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item requesting a refund. Always present in a valid refund request.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Description of the reason for the refund request. Must be at least 5 characters and provide a clear justification for the refund.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was soft-deleted. Null indicates the request is still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical records capturing previous status values for order items, created on every status change. Preserves detailed context for audit trails and historical tracking without modification.

This table stores every state transition of order items, including the exact previous status value and timestamp when the change occurred. Snapshots are created automatically during status change operations without user intervention, ensuring an accurate and unalterable history for all order item status modifications.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item that was modified. Reference to shopping_mall_order_items.id

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: Previous status value before the change occurred. Tracks the exact state prior to the modification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created (when status change occurred).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was last updated. (Never changes for snapshots, but required by standard pattern.)

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the snapshot was marked as deleted. (Snapshots are immutable, so this is not used in practice but maintained for consistency.)

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Customer cancellation requests for specific order items with reason and approval workflow.

Stores cancellation requests initiated by customers for specific order items within the shopping mall platform.
Each request includes a reason for cancellation and follows a formal approval workflow managed by sellers or administrators.

The cancellation workflow supports multiple statuses including 'pending', 'approved', and 'rejected'.
When rejected, the request includes a reason for the rejection.

All requests are timestamped to track request creation and approval timelines.
Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails for completed cancellations.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item for which cancellation is requested. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason specified for order item cancellation. May include details about the order item or customer's concern.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of cancellation request. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected. Status transitions follow business workflow rules.

plainFields.name: approved_by_id
plainFields.description: User who approved the cancellation request. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id} or {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: rejected_reason
plainFields.description: Reason specified for rejecting the cancellation request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of cancellation request creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last cancellation request modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of cancellation request deletion (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_account_status_histories
models.description:
Tracks historical status changes for seller accounts (pending, approved, rejected) with associated timestamps and approval reasons.

This table captures the history of seller account status transitions from the initial registration status through approval or rejection process. Each change is recorded with the exact timestamp and approval reason provided by the administrator.

The table is designed as a snapshot to preserve historical data without altering current account status, enabling full audit trail of seller account validation process. This implementation strictly follows snapshot pattern requirements by capturing complete state changes rather than incremental updates.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller account this history record belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status transition (one of: pending, approved, rejected). Valid values must match the enum from seller status.

plainFields.name: approval_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for approval or rejection provided by the administrator during status change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the status change was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this history record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was soft deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical records capturing changes to seller profile data including shop name and logo modifications.

Each snapshot preserves the prior values before the change and the current values after the change, allowing full traceability of profile evolution.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever seller profile data is modified and are intended for audit purposes only. These records cannot be edited or deleted after creation but can be viewed by seller owners and system administrators.

The table maintains full historical context through references to the main seller account (shopping_mall_sellers.id) and includes comprehensive fields for tracking both before and after profile values for shop name and logo.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller profile being snapshotted. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated (should match created_at for immutable records).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was deleted (soft delete for historical record management).

plainFields.name: previous_shop_name
plainFields.description: Previous shop name before change.

plainFields.name: new_shop_name
plainFields.description: New shop name after change.

plainFields.name: previous_logo_url
plainFields.description: Previous logo URL before change.

plainFields.name: new_logo_url
plainFields.description: New logo URL after change.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Active wishlist entries linking customers to products without variant specificity.

Stores individual product references that customers have added to their wishlist for easy access and future purchase considerations. Each entry represents a direct link between a customer and a product, without any variant specificity. The product reference preserves historical information even if the product later changes or is deleted, as the snapshot system handles that detail.

Entries remain active until explicitly removed by the customer or automatically removed when a product is deleted from the catalog. Active entries are visible to the customer in their wishlist interface, while deleted entries are preserved in snapshots but not shown in the active listings.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer's identity. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product being wishlisted. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist item was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If deleted, timestamp of deletion for soft delete functionality.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots preserving deleted products from customer wishlists for historical reference.

Captures the exact wishlist item state and associated product information at the moment a product is removed from a seller's catalog, ensuring customer wishlist history remains intact. Each snapshot records the product data that existed when the product was deleted, preserving it for audit trails and historical analysis.

Snapshots are automatically created when a product is deleted from the catalog, referencing the specific wishlist item that contained the deleted product. They serve as permanent records for customer review history and order fulfillment verification, supporting the system's snapshot policy requirements.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_item_id
foreignFields.description: Wishlist item's {@link shopping_mall_wishlist_items.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp. Records when the wishlist item was captured in its historical state.
